description: Painting in ground mineral pigments fixed with animal glue, on paper or silk, in the Japanese tradition.
A small painted portrait made as a work of its own, often on vellum, ivory, card or metal.
An image hand-painted in acrylic on a clear acetate sheet, made for an animated film.
An image sprayed onto paper, canvas or another sheet by a print head with pigment or dye inks.
An ornamental figure cast in pewter, zinc, tin or another non-bronze metal.
Script characters carved into a seal of stone or another material as a work of art, sold as the seal or its impressions.
A base, plinth or stand made for one sculpture.
An image made by pressing damp paper into a carved or built-up plate so the design stands in relief, mainly without ink. Embossing added to an inked print is not this.
